scope: Theorem 1.2 (Parity reduction) of the manuscript “Parity lifts and bounded-treewidth witnesses for Weisfeiler–Leman equivalence” (preprints/Parity-lifts-and-bounded-treewidth-witnesses-for-Weisfeiler-Leman-equivalence-September-25-2026/paper.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 133 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 742b4b63acfcfeec), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 2. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: Fix k ≥ 4, either refinement convention, and the corresponding t in (1.1). From every choice system on t domains one can explicitly construct two uncolored simple graphs X0, X⋆ of equal order such that X0 ≡k X⋆ ⇐⇒ the choice system has no successful choice. The assertion holds both with common color names on separate graphs and with pure-tuple comparison in their disjoint union. If every domain and label set has size at most A, where A ≥ 1, their common order is at most AMt, where Mt = t 2t−2+3(t−1 2 ) + 12 t 3 ! . When a successful choice exists, the two graphs already have different histograms after at most two joint rounds, or one separate round.
